messages.author: ccbcef3bee6c8b59
messages.subject: Error in diroutput
parts:
Hi,

We have encountered an error in Part 5. 

Error in dir.exists(outputdir) : invalid filename argument

This is our entire script
library(GGIR)

#set working directory
setwd("~/Dataverwerking thesis")
datadir="C:/Users/jessi/Documents/Dataverwerking thesis/Data"
outputdir="C:/Users/jessi/Documents/Dataverwerking thesis"
g.shell.GGIR(
  #=====================
  # Part 1
  #=====================
  mode=c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), #welke parts moeten geanalyseerd worden
  datadir=datadir,
  outputdir=outputdir,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  do.parallel = TRUE,
  idloc = 1, #welke bestandsnaam we kiezen
  do.report=c(2, 4, 5), #voeg 4 en 5 toe
  do.enmo = TRUE,  
 
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1,#welke tijdsduur je gebruikt - 1 betekent de ganse metingstijd
  hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 1,
  # protocol specific --> my protocol --> the devices start measuring at
  # 8pm and at 8am the next day, the participant starts to wear the device.  
  # RE: Correct, additionally, specify excludefirst.part4 = TRUE, to make sure
  # first night is ignored for sleep detection
  GGIR(includedaycrit = 16, #eens navragen bij Nicky of Maite welke criteria ze hanteren,
  # why is this the same for includedaycrit and includenightcrit?
  # RE: Both consider a 24 hour window. includedaycrit looks at midnight-midnight
  # includenightcrit looks at noon-noon
  qwindow ="C:/Users/jessi/Documents/Dataverwerking thesis/testh.csv",
  qwindow_dateformat = "%d-%m-%Y",            
  mvpathreshold =c(100)),
  # bout.metric = 6,
  # Which bout.metric do you recommend for a 24hour analysis?
  # RE: Do not specify, which means that it uses the default, which is 6.
# bout.metric kies 6, anders te ingewikkeld
  includenightcrit = 16,
  # if we want to do a 24h analysis --> is it better to use
  # includedaycrit = 10 and includenightcrit = 6 or should we use for both 16h?
  # RE: 16 is in both cases relative to a 24 hour window
  visualreport = TRUE,
  dofirstpage = TRUE,
 

  # Part 3+4
  #=====================
  timethreshold= c(1), #mogelijks nog aan te passen, stond oorspronkelijk p 5 als default
  anglethreshold=5,
  ignorenonwear = FALSE,
  excludefirst.part4 = FALSE,
  # this parameter will exclude the first night but we want to exclude
  # the first Waking-Waking window. Is it possible to do
  # excludefirst.part5 for a WW window?  
  # RE: No, see documentation => excludefirstlast.part5
  # But maybe do hrs.del.start = 20 which means 8pm - 4pm
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  # using the algorithm with no sleeplog information
  # RE: Correct
 
  # Part 5 #
  #=====================
  threshold.lig=c(30), threshold.mod=c(100), threshold.vig=c(400),
  # Thresholds in hilderbrand 2014 differ from the Hildebrand 2016?  
  # RE: 2014 focusses on MVPA, 2016 on SB
  boutcriter = 0.8 , boutcriter.in = 0.8, boutcriter.lig = 0.8, boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
  # How do you define the boutcrit??
  # RE: No strict rules as there is hardly literature on this. It is mainly matter
  # of interpretation.
  boutdur.in = c(1),
  boutdur.lig = c(1),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  # how do you define the boutdur?
  # RE: Population and research question specific.
  #
  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
  timewindow = c("MM"),
  dayborder = 3,
  visualreport=TRUE,
  frag.metrics = "mean",
  part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE
  )

Can you help us?

Thank you!
Kind regards
Jessie

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Error in diroutput
parts:
Hi Jessie,

The error doesn't seem to be related to part 5, but to the definition of the outputdir. Can you check the outputdir exists and is correctly defined? Why do you think it is related to part 5? Did you get the output for parts 1 to 4 as expected?

Best,
Jairo
